chapter: Teens with the Salt City Six
title: Joining the Salt City Six at 15 and going on the road at 16
summary: After mononucleosis he is called to Memory Lane in Syracuse; his parents let him tour with Jack Maheu and Will Alger as minders, with predictable results.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: No Joe was gone by then. But the drummer that I did see there was Jake Hanna. And that was my first meeting with Jake. But let’s see, okay, so anyway, let’s get back to when I was 15, during that summer break, I had played with the band, okay, in the fall, at age 15 I had been released from my medical restrictions because of the mononucleosis, to go back to school. The phone rings and now they want me to play at Memory Lane with the Salt City Six. And now this job went on, they used to go from nine to one or nine to two in those days. I of course never made school on Monday morning. And here I am now playing, and I wasn’t even legally allowed to in those days, because you’re not supposed to be playing in gin mills. That was a law. But I looked a little old for my age, like I do now. But one time my homeroom teacher came in and he says, “now I know why you’re never at school on Monday mornings.” He said, “that’s all right I like jazz, I’ll cover for you.” But anyway, so that summer they called and they said, “we want you to go on the road with us permanently, we’re going on the road.” So that was a decision. My mother was, “oh no you can’t, no you’re not going on the road at age 16” or whatever it was. And I was begging. I says, “man, I’m not mowing lawns, I’m not doing anything, I’m not playing Friday nights.” I didn’t play with the school dance band because why play for 3 dollars at the YMCA when I could be making 15 — well it was 12 to 15 to 18 dollars with my father’s band or Spiegle’s band, or whatever band. Anyway my father said, he said, “okay we’re going to let him go but we’re going to put him in charge of Jack Maheu and Will Alger, that they’ll watch out for him.” That was like letting the hen guard — the fox guarding the henhouse. These guys, man I was loaded constantly with these guys. Now they’re going to Pennsylvania to play at the Penn Sheraton and the legal drinking age is 21 there. Now 18 here. See that means it’s all changed in New York State as you know.
